q: A chemist wants to know whether a colourless liquid is pure ethanol or ethanol mixed with water. Which result best shows it is a mixture?
options: The anhydrous copper(II) sulfate turns blue.
explain: Pure ethanol would not turn anhydrous copper(II) sulfate blue; a colour change shows water is present.

q: Which pair of substances in water both harm aquatic life?
options: minerals from metal compounds and dissolved oxygen
explain: Plastics harm aquatic life and sewage brings harmful microbes; dissolved oxygen and essential minerals are beneficial.

q: Which statement about adding anhydrous copper(II) sulfate to a liquid is correct?
options: It turns pink if the liquid is pure water.
It turns blue only if the liquid is pure water.
It shows the boiling point of the liquid.
It only shows that water is present, not that the water is pure.
explain: The test is for the presence of water; it cannot tell pure water from solutions.

q: In a purity check a student finds that a liquid melts at −5 °C. Which statement is correct if the liquid is supposed to be pure water?
options: The water is impure because its melting point is below 0 °C.
The water is pure because water melts below 0 °C.
The water is impure because its melting point is above 0 °C.
The water is pure because it is liquid.
explain: Pure water melts at exactly 0 °C; a lower melting point shows dissolved impurities.

q: A water company uses carbon in a filter bed. What property of the carbon makes it suitable?
options: It kills microbes by releasing chlorine.
It removes substances that cause bad taste and smell.
It settles out large solid particles.
It adds minerals to the water.
explain: Carbon removes the substances responsible for unpleasant tastes and odours; microbes are killed by chlorine.

q: Which statement about tap water and distilled water is correct?
options: Distilled water contains more dissolved substances than tap water.
Tap water and distilled water contain the same chemicals.
Tap water contains more dissolved substances than distilled water.
Distilled water contains dissolved oxygen but tap water does not.
explain: Tap water contains dissolved substances; distillation removes them.

q: Which of these is a source of harmful microbes in natural water?
explain: Sewage contains microbes that cause disease.

q: Which compound is used as a fertiliser?
explain: Ammonium salts and nitrates supply nitrogen to plants.

q: Which three elements are provided by an NPK fertiliser?
explain: N, P and K are the symbols for nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium.

q: Why do farmers add fertilisers to soil?
options: to kill harmful microbes in the soil
to replace elements that crops have removed so plants grow better
to add carbon dioxide to the air
explain: Crops take up nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium from soil; fertilisers replace them for improved growth.

q: Which of these is an ammonium salt that is used as a fertiliser?
explain: (NH₄)₂SO₄ is ammonium sulfate and contains the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺, which provides nitrogen.

q: Which formula is ammonium nitrate?
explain: Ammonium nitrate contains the NH₄⁺ ion and the NO₃⁻ ion in a 1 : 1 ratio.

q: Which row correctly matches the symbol with the element in NPK fertilisers?
explain: N is nitrogen, P is phosphorus and K is potassium.

q: What is meant by an NPK fertiliser?
options: a fertiliser containing compounds of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium
a fertiliser made from sodium, phosphorus and krypton
a fertiliser that adds only potassium
explain: NPK fertilisers supply all three of the elements needed for improved plant growth.

q: Potassium nitrate is used as a fertiliser. Which elements does it provide?
explain: KNO₃ contains potassium and nitrogen (in the nitrate ion).

q: Which statement about fertilisers is correct?
options: Fertilisers must dissolve in water so that plant roots can absorb them.
Fertilisers are made only from metals.
Fertilisers remove nitrogen from the soil.
explain: Plants absorb nutrients dissolved in water through their roots.

q: Excess fertiliser is washed from fields into a river. Which problem may this cause?
options: Nitrates and phosphates reduce the oxygen in the water.
Chlorine is formed in the water.
explain: Nitrates and phosphates lead to deoxygenation of water.

q: Which of the following is NOT used as a fertiliser?
explain: Sodium chloride does not supply N, P or K in a form useful to plants.

q: Ammonium phosphate, (NH₄)₃PO₄, is used as a fertiliser. Which elements does it supply?
explain: (NH₄)₃PO₄ contains nitrogen (in NH₄⁺) and phosphorus (in PO₄³⁻).

q: What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen in ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃? (Ar: H = 1, N = 14, O = 16)
explain: Mr = 14 + 4 + 14 + 48 = 80. The two N atoms have mass 28, so 28 ÷ 80 × 100 = 35%.

q: Which fertiliser has the highest percentage by mass of nitrogen? (Ar: H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32)
explain: NH₄NO₃: 28/80 = 35%; (NH₄)₂SO₄: 28/132 = 21%; NH₄Cl: 14/53.5 = 26%; (NH₄)₃PO₄: 42/149 = 28%, so NH₄NO₃ is highest.

q: Ammonia reacts with sulfuric acid to make the fertiliser ammonium sulfate. Which equation is correct?
explain: Two NH₃ each gain one H⁺ to form 2NH₄⁺, which pair with one SO₄²⁻.

q: Which equation represents the formation of the fertiliser ammonium nitrate from ammonia?
explain: One NH₃ accepts one H⁺ from HNO₃ to give NH₄⁺ and NO₃⁻.

q: A bag contains 40 kg of ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃. What mass of nitrogen does it contain? (Ar: H = 1, N = 14, O = 16)
explain: Mr = 80 and N is 28/80 = 35% of the mass, so 0.35 × 40 = 14 kg.

q: A student warms a fertiliser with sodium hydroxide solution and a gas is released that turns damp red litmus paper blue. Which ion is present in the fertiliser?
explain: Ammonium ions react with warm sodium hydroxide to release ammonia, an alkaline gas that turns damp red litmus blue.

q: Which statement explains why a farmer might use ammonium nitrate rather than potassium chloride on a field lacking nitrogen?
options: Potassium chloride contains nitrogen but ammonium nitrate does not.
Ammonium nitrate contains nitrogen but potassium chloride does not.
Ammonium nitrate is insoluble but potassium chloride is soluble.
Potassium chloride has a higher percentage of nitrogen.
explain: Plants need nitrogen compounds; KCl contains no nitrogen.

q: Which row correctly lists a fertiliser and the elements from NPK that it provides?
explain: (NH₄)₂HPO₄ has ammonium nitrogen and phosphate phosphorus; KNO₃ gives N and K, NH₄NO₃ gives only N, KCl gives only K.

q: What is the approximate percentage of nitrogen in clean, dry air?
explain: Clean, dry air is approximately 78% nitrogen, N₂.

q: Which gas makes up approximately 21% of clean, dry air?
explain: Oxygen, O₂, is about 21% of clean, dry air.

q: Which row correctly gives the approximate composition of clean, dry air?
explain: Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, with the remainder noble gases and carbon dioxide.
